item.title: Beyond Line of Sight: How Part 108 Could Transform Commercial Drones
item.description: The FAA’s proposed Part 108 rule could unlock routine beyond-visual-line-of-sight drone operations, transforming emergency response, infrastructure inspection, and logistics. But getting the safety architecture right will determine whether the United States leads the next era of autonomous aviation.

item.title: Tracking FY 2027 Defense Appropriations, Reconciliation, and the Supplemental Request
item.description: As the October 1 start of the fiscal year (FY) approaches, Congress has yet to take enact defense funding for FY 2027. Seamus Daniels outlines the current status of legislation in response to the Trump administration’s $1.5 trillion defense budget request.

item.title: Mapping Iranian Cyberattacks on U.S. Water Systems
item.description: Recent Iranian cyberattacks on U.S. water systems were months in the making. These charts combine press reporting and CSIS expert analysis to provide a clearer picture of the attacks and their impact on the U.S. water sector.

item.title: The Implications of Japan’s New National Intelligence Bureau
item.description: Japan’s new National Intelligence Bureau is an important early step in Japanese intelligence reform and creates opportunities for deeper cooperation with the United States and other partners.

item.title: Are SBIR “Mills” Truly a Problem?
item.description: The Small Business Innovation Research Program has faced suggestions that a small number of “mills” receive a disproportionate share of awards while underperforming on innovation and commercialization metrics. An analysis of grant recipient data suggests this pattern reflects a division between specialized defense research contractors and dual-use venture-backed companies.

item.title: After Iran: A Scenario for Renewed Trump-Kim Summitry
item.description: Why would North Korea’s leader be interested in more summits with Trump? If Kim Jong-un is a revisionist in his outlook, he would look to capitalize on any available opportunity to advance the core goal of cementing his status as a nuclear weapons state, argues Victor Cha.

item.title: The Value of U.S. Land Power
item.description: Drones, AI, and long-range fires are reshaping warfare, but land power remains vital to achieving political and strategic objectives. CSIS’s Future of Land Power study examines why ground forces endure—and how they must adapt for future conflict as part of the joint force.

item.title: Emergency Episode: What's Happening with Korea? Military exercises, Kim Jong-un and Iran
item.description: On an emergency episode of the Capital Cable, experts discuss U.S-North Korea relations, joint military exercises and a potential Trump-Kim meeting.

item.title: The Cyberattacks on the U.S Water Sector and the Iran Question: Escalation or Opportunism?
item.description: It is highly likely that Iran is behind the cyberattacks on the U.S. water sector. Psychological effect—not escalation—is the point of Iran’s cyber operations, to sow fear, chaos, and division as part of its information warfare strategy.

item.title: Is a New Chinese Runway Taking Flight at Antelope Reef?
item.description: China begins construction at Antelope Reef.
